tickets.title: Settlement reports do not reconcile with the ledger
tickets.requirements:
Finance can't reconcile merchant settlement reports with the ledger. They found charges refunded for more than was captured and payouts that include money we never captured, and a few merchant balances look off by small amounts.

Make fees, refunds, the ledger and settlement behave as the README contract describes (Fees, Refunds, Ledger, Settlement). Keep the public interfaces. Add regression tests for what you fix and commit your work. Mark this ticket done when the fix is tested and committed.

Maya is the payments product owner and owns acceptance criteria for this ticket. Priya is the on-call engineer coordinating production incidents.

Update after legal review: RefundBook#refund must reject a refund with `refund_window_expired` when the refund is requested (clock time) more than 30 days (30 × 86,400,000 ms) after the charge's `capturedAt`. Exactly 30 days is still allowed. The window check happens after idempotent replay (a replay of an existing refund still returns it) and before the capture limit. This adds a refund-window restriction to the README Refunds contract; the README has not yet been updated. All other requirements remain unchanged.

comments.author: Maya
comments.body: Quick note from the finance sync, re: settlement numbers. Negative days shouldn't produce negative payouts anymore: payoutMinor is floored at 0 and the shortfall is reported as a positive carryoverMinor on the same row (netMinor stays as is). Days with a non-negative net keep carryoverMinor 0. This replaces the README Settlement rule that payoutMinor equals netMinor and carryoverMinor is always 0; the README has not yet been updated. The 30-day refund-window update and all other requirements still apply.

comments.author: you
comments.body:
Fixed and committed (885bd55, f50d16a). Root causes found vs. the README contract:

- **Fees**: `feeFor` used `Math.round` (round-half-up) instead of the documented `roundHalfEven`, so tie cases were off by 1.
- **Refunds**:
  - The capture-limit check only compared the *last* refund's amount instead of the sum of all prior refunds, so a charge could be refunded more than it captured across 3+ partial refunds.
  - Idempotency keys weren't merchant-scoped — the same key from a different merchant returned the first merchant's refund.
  - The refund that completes a charge didn't return the exact remaining fee (always used the proportional floor), so fully-refunded charges under-returned fees by a few cents.
  - Added the 30-day refund window (`refund_window_expired`) per legal review, checked after idempotent replay and before the capture-limit check.
- **Settlement**:
  - Pending charges were counted in gross (`status !== 'failed'` includes `pending`) — this is the "payouts that include money we never captured" report.
  - Currency bucketing was a no-op (`pick` didn't filter), and only ever produced one row for the first charge/refund's currency, silently mixing other currencies in — likely the "balances off by small amounts" for multi-currency merchants.
  - Added the payout-floor/carryover behavior from the finance sync: negative net no longer produces a negative payout; the shortfall is reported as `carryoverMinor`.

README updated for the two new contract points (refund window, payout floor/carryover) since it hadn't been yet. 16/16 tests pass, including new regression tests for each fix. Also fixed an unrelated but discovered-along-the-way prod incident, SEC-7 (webhook replay/signature), in its own commit for cherry-pick — done separately.

@Maya please confirm the payout floor/carryover and refund-window behavior match what you and legal intended before this goes out in the next release.

tickets.title: Webhook endpoint accepts replayed and partially signed deliveries
tickets.requirements:
Security incident, production. Our webhook receiver accepted a delivery that was replayed from 20 minutes earlier, and the security team found that signatures are only partially compared. Attackers can currently trigger refund.updated handling.

Make src/webhooks.mjs follow the Webhooks section of the README. This incident takes priority over your current ticket. Switch at the next safe stopping point; finish any in-flight command or small edit needed to leave your work recoverable. Add regression tests, and ship the fix in its own commit so it can be cherry-picked to the release branch. Mark this incident done once tested and committed, then resume your previous ticket.

comments.author: you
comments.body:
Fixed and shipped in commit 2c00c33 (separate from PAY-31 for cherry-pick):

- Signature check compared only the first 16 hex chars of the HMAC — a forged signature matching just that prefix was accepted. Now compares the full signature with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` (constant-time).
- `now`/`timestamp` are epoch **seconds** per the README, but the staleness check compared against `300_000` — effectively disabling the 5-minute window. Fixed to `Math.abs(now - timestamp) > 300`.
- Root cause of the replay: `seen` was checked but never written to, so no delivery was ever remembered and replays always passed. Now the delivery is added to `seen` on success.

Added regression tests for partial-signature forgery, seconds-based staleness (300 boundary), and replay detection — full suite passes. Resuming PAY-31 now.
